questions.prompt: A write-heavy workload slows down because every write updates many secondary indexes.
questions.explanation: Reduce unnecessary indexes or choose a write-optimized design. In DDIA: Storage and Retrieval, the first move is to protect the system's real guarantee: match storage engine to workload.
options: Reduce unnecessary indexes or choose a write-optimized design
questions.answer: Reduce unnecessary indexes or choose a write-optimized design

concept_panel.title: LSM Trees and SSTables
concept_panel.explanation: LSM-style storage writes data to an in-memory memtable and append-only logs, then flushes sorted immutable files called SSTables. Compaction later merges files and removes obsolete entries. This design can be strong for write-heavy workloads but may add read amplification. The interview point is understanding the read/write trade-off in storage engines.
key_takeaways: Compaction trades background work for efficient storage.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you understand storage-engine trade-offs beyond SQL syntax.
concept_panel.practical_example: A write-heavy event store may favor an LSM engine, while a read-heavy index lookup may favor B-tree behavior.
